title: Philippines extends 2-week visa-free entry for Chinese nationals
summary: The DFA says the move is 'in line with the President's directive to boost international tourist arrivals and investments'

items: The Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry for Chinese nationals until January 15, 2028, to boost tourism and investments.
The visa-free entry applies only to arrivals at Ninoy Aquino International Airport and Mactan-Cebu International Airport, with specific requirements for travelers.
This extension occurs amid ongoing tensions between the Philippines and China over territorial claims in the South China Sea.

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) announced Monday, November 23, that the Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry for Chinese nationals for another year or until January 15, 2028. The temporary visa-free rule covers Chinese nationals flying into the Philippines for tourism or travel. It was introduced in January 2026.

“The extension is in line with the President’s directive to boost international tourist arrivals and investments in the Philippines, while maintaining existing immigration and national security safeguards,” said the DFA in a statement.

The visa-free privilege covers only entries via Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Metro Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport (MCIA) in Cebu. Chinese nationals should have a passport valid for at least six months beyond their stay in the Philippines and should have hotel bookings, as well as existing tickets to leave the Philippines.

“Further, admission into the Philippines remains subject to inspection, screening procedures, and determination by the BI, including applicable identity verification, watchlist checks, and risk based assessment. The DFA will continue to coordinate with the BI and the law enforcement agencies on the monitoring of the implementation of the 14-day visa-free arrangement for Chinese nationals,” added the DFA. Chinese travelers who are only transiting through the Philippines should obtain a transit visa.

The Philippines has been trying to boost its tourism and investment numbers, including through granting specific nationals conditional visa-free entry. Manila allows Indian nationals to enter for 14 or 30 days without a visa. It also has a similar arrangement with Taiwan, a democratically-governed island that China sees as its own.

The extension of the visa-free privilege happens despite increased tensions between the two countries — diplomatically and at sea. Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, including parts that are within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone. Competing claims have meant increasingly tense confrontations between maritime personnel of both countries. The Philippines has said its bilateral ties with China exist beyond maritime issues. – Rappler.com
